llm_30m_sig_phrase: not statistically different from zero (the 95% CI includes zero)
llm_half_life_phrase: falls below half its 5-minute level by the 30 min horizon
ratio_30m: not meaningful, because the FinBERT IC is not distinguishable from zero
llm_vs_finbert_verdict: The LLM did not beat FinBERT by a statistically reliable margin at 30 minutes: the paired bootstrap CI on the difference includes zero.
latency_death_phrase: The strategy is net-negative at every entry delay tested, including zero.
latency_gross_phrase: Gross edge is still positive at 900 seconds.
killer_phrase: The signal first, then costs. At the 30-minute exit the gross edge is +6.1 bps per trade with a 95% CI of [-8.8, +20.0], so it cannot be told apart from zero. Costs then remove any doubt: 18.3 bps per round trip (10 bps of fees, 8.3 bps of estimated spread), and even with zero fees the net edge is -2.2 bps.
latency_ic_phrase: the CI excludes zero only at 0 s and 60 s
post_run_notes:
- **Most headlines carry no signal, and pooling them buries what little there is.** {{share_other}} of OOS events fall in the `other` category, {{share_near_zero}} get an LLM sentiment within 0.1 of zero, and {{share_conf_low}} get confidence of 0.4 or less. A pooled IC over that population measures the noise as much as the model.
- **The LLM's confidence did not sort the signal.** The highest-confidence bucket does not have a higher IC than the lowest. A score that knew when it was right would have made the trade filter work; this one did not.
- **The LLM did not beat FinBERT by a margin this sample can detect.** Both are close to zero at every horizon, and the paired CIs on the difference all include zero.
- **The embedding baseline is a puzzle, not a win.** Its in-sample CV AUC was {{embed_cv_auc}}, near chance, yet it posts the only pooled IC whose CI excludes zero ({{embed_sig_phrase}}). With {{n_ic_tests}} model-by-horizon tests, one or two marginal CIs are expected by chance. A plausible mechanism is that it learned headline form (recaps of moves already under way) rather than sentiment, but I have not tested that.
- **The pre-specified primary horizon was the weakest one.** I fixed the 30-minute exit before seeing any OOS data. After the fact, the 5-minute exit is the only configuration with a gross edge that clears zero, but it comes from headlines traded at the open, and choosing it now would be fitting to the OOS sample.
- **Overnight news is priced by the open.** Headlines that arrive outside market hours have an LLM IC of {{ic_sess_overnight}} from the next open. The opening auction absorbs them before a retail-speed trader can act.
- **One-at-a-time LLM scoring was needlessly expensive.** Re-sending the 5,000-token prompt for every headline cost about ${{single_usd_per_1k}} per 1,000 events. Batching 20 headlines per request through the Batches API brought that to ${{batch_usd_per_1k}}.
- **Deduplication barely mattered.** The near-duplicate filter removed only {{dropped_near_duplicates}} headlines; Benzinga already deduplicates its feed.
